tones.name: 3rd tone
tones.shape: low, dipping; in speech mostly just low

rows.r: y (spelling for i- at the start)
w (spelling for u- at the start)
as in "or" (after b p m f)
"ü" + "e" (written ue after j q x y)
"ü" + "an" (written uan after j q x y)
"ü" + "n" (written un after j q x y)

notes.en: Two 3rd tones in a row: the first is spoken as a 2nd tone. 你好 is written nǐ hǎo but said ní hǎo. The written marks do not change.
Before any other tone, a 3rd tone is usually just low (it does not rise again): 老师 lǎoshī = low + high.
不 is bù, but bú before a 4th tone: 不是 bú shì, 不对 bú duì. In verb + 不 + verb it is neutral: 是不是 shì bu shì. This course writes the tone that is spoken.
一 is yī alone, when counting and in dates; yí before a 4th tone (一个 yí ge, 一样 yíyàng); yì before tones 1-3 (一天 yì tiān, 一起 yìqǐ). This course writes the tone that is spoken.
Neutral tone: short and light, written without a mark. Particles (吗 ma, 的 de, 了 le), noun suffixes (子 zi, 们 men) and the second half of many words (谢谢 xièxie, 朋友 péngyou).
After j, q, x and y the two dots of ü are dropped: 去 qù, 学 xué, 鱼 yú all have ü. After n and l they stay: 女 nǚ, 绿 lǜ (because nu and lu also exist).
Shortened spellings: iou is written iu (六 liù), uei is written ui (对 duì), uen is written un (春 chūn).
At the start of a syllable i- is written y and u- is written w: ia = ya, uo = wo, i = yi, u = wu, ü = yu.
The i in zhi, chi, shi, ri, zi, ci, si is not "ee": it is a buzzing continuation of the consonant.
An apostrophe separates syllables when the next one starts with a, o or e: 西安 Xī'ān (two syllables), not xiān.
Where the mark goes: on a or e if present; on o in ou; otherwise on the last vowel (liù, duì).
Northern r-ending: 哪儿 nǎr, 一点儿 yìdiǎnr, 玩儿 wánr. The 儿 adds an r sound to the syllable before it.
b d g are not voiced like English b d g; they are plain p t k without a puff of air. p t k have a strong puff.

quizzes.label: zh z j, ch c q, sh s x, r l
quizzes.hint: Curled tongue (zh ch sh r), flat tongue (z c s), or tongue tip down behind the teeth (j q x)?

quizzes.label: u or ü (spelling)
quizzes.hint: After j, q, x and y a written u is really ü.

quizzes.hint: Does the syllable end in -n (tongue up front) or -ng (back of the throat)?
